verses.text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jerushah, daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Uzziah had done. But he did not go into the LORD's temple as his father had. The people, however, kept on doing wrong.
Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the LORD's temple and did a lot of building on the wall at Ophel.
He built towns in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers in the forest areas.

He fought against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him about three and a half tonnes of silver, ten thousand loads of wheat, and ten thousand loads of barley. They paid him the same amount in the second and third years.
Jotham became powerful because he lived carefully, obeying the LORD his God.
Everything else Jotham did, including all his wars and his ways, is written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham died and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king after him.
